title: perf(canary): auto-detect regressions and add rollout guards for latency/throughput
author: Anika Sharma
description: Motivation: Recent incidents showed undetected small regressions in tail latency and throughput after model rollouts. This PR implements continuous canary detection for latency and throughput regressions and adds automatic rollout guards to block or rollback unsafe rollouts. Changes: 1) A new detector pipeline (perf-canary/detectors) that computes rolling quantiles and throughput baselines per route and model; 2) An adaptive alert algorithm that combines statistically-significant drift detection (CUSUM) with traffic-aware thresholds; 3) Rollout guard controller integrated with the rollout service to pause/cancel canary promotions when detectors trigger; 4) Console UI hooks and a metrics-backed history for debugging; 5) E2E tests and perf benchmarks. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve existing canary behavior; rollout guards are opt-in per-release via config. Checklist: [x] design doc updated, [x] unit + integration tests, [x] perf canary benchmarks, [x] console UI affordances, [x] add flag for opt-in rollout guards. Risk: false positives could block rollouts; mitigations include automatic backoff, staged thresholds, and manual override. How validated: synthetic workloads simulating tail latency spikes (p99 increase of 30%); throughput flood tests; end-to-end integration in perf-canary lab for 48h. Rollout plan: feature-flagged release to staging for 2 weeks, then gradual enable for <10% of production routes, monitor for false positives, then enable by default. References: ENG-3784 design, SUP-2231 customer incident, prior canary PRs for baseline extraction.

release_notes: Add automatic canary regression detection for latency and throughput.
Introduce rollout guards that can pause/rollback rollouts when regressions are detected.
Feature is behind a per-release opt-in flag; see docs/observability/canary-rollout-guards.md for configuration.
perf_bench_summary: Benchmarks in perf-canary lab: detector overhead measured at <2% CPU on 16 core node under 1k RPS; rolling-quantile update optimized to O(1) amortized; in synthetic regression injection tests, the guard prevented 100% of canary-promotions with p99+ increases >=25% and 95% of promotions with p99 increases >=15% when thresholds enabled.
